blocks.content: This module surveys deployment strategies as a family, this topic revisits rolling update, Kubernetes's native default, specifically to weigh its real tradeoffs against the other three strategies covered alongside it.

The actual mechanics, gradual replacement, maxSurge, maxUnavailable, are covered in full in the Deployments module's Rolling Updates topic, this topic assumes that foundation and focuses on where it fits among the broader strategy landscape.

blocks.alt: The mechanics live elsewhere, this topic is about strategic positioning

blocks.content: 2. The Real Advantage: No Extra Infrastructure
blocks.text: 2. The Real Advantage: No Extra Infrastructure

blocks.content: Rolling update's biggest practical strength is that it requires nothing beyond a standard Deployment, no second environment, no traffic-splitting infrastructure, it is simply how Deployments already behave by default.

blocks.alt: Genuinely free, requiring no additional infrastructure investment at all

blocks.content: This is the tradeoff worth stating plainly: during a rolling update, old and new versions genuinely run simultaneously, for applications with backward-incompatible changes, a new database schema the old code cannot handle, for instance, this overlap can be a genuine problem, not just a theoretical one.

blocks.alt: A real, active overlap period, not a purely theoretical concern

blocks.content: If something goes wrong mid-rollout, reverting is itself a gradual process, covered in the Rollback topic, there is no instant "flip back to exactly how it was a moment ago," a real limitation compared to the pattern covered in the Blue-Green topic later in this module.

blocks.alt: A gradual reversal, not an instant one, worth knowing before you need it

blocks.content: 5. Where It Fits Among the Four Strategies
blocks.text: 5. Where It Fits Among the Four Strategies

blocks.content: Rolling update is the sensible default for the large majority of stateless applications, free, built-in, and safe enough for changes that can tolerate a brief version overlap, the other three strategies in this module exist for the specific cases this default does not fit well.

blocks.alt: The sensible default, with the other three strategies covering its specific gaps

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Rolling update's real advantage is needing no extra infrastructure at all, it is simply how Deployments already work by default.
Its real cost is a genuine overlap between old and new versions during the rollout, and no instant way to revert, worth weighing against the other strategies in this module.
